# Chapter One: Marcus

> *"Honor is the first of the four tenets. It is the measure by which all men are judged."*
> — **Book of Aurtus**

“Am I home?” his voice still suffering the effects of the chemicals used in reanimation, Marcus’s mouth uttering a scratchy low whisper, sounding more like an old man of one hundred rather than the spry twenty-seven he was.

He paused in surprise, that isn’t my voice, is it? he wondered, blinking back fresh tears as sunlight seared retinas that had not felt the light for a millennium, his vision slowly coming back into focus, the fuzzy green and brown blobs of color sharpening into the technicolor of autumn leaves, looking up he surveyed the pastel canvas splayed across the forest canopy, a sound like dry parchment echoing through the trees, as branches swayed in time to the rising breeze.

Earth, he thought with a relieved sigh beginning to relax, fear dissipating, replaced with familiarity, the deep ache from joints that had not been used in centuries complained as he willed his body to move.

Turning he studied the remnants of the silver teardrop shaped craft half buried at the end of a long ravine created when it had hit the ground. How long have I been away? He wondered looking to the surrounding fauna for answers, but none came.

Marcus winced as his muscles protested in pain, testing his strength. The one-piece gortex outfit he wore stretching with the movements of his body, the restriction of the outfit causing him to scowl in annoyance.

After such a long period of Cryogenic sleep, your body will require a period to adjust, though your entire being will be frozen, ensuring you do not age while waiting for your return home we anticipate certain unpleasant side effects that you will have to overcome upon awakening a familiar voice echoed from his mind, a holdover from his now distant past. Here I am he thought, a smile replacing the annoyed wince as he studied the lush forest before him.

Marcus had spent time in forests, mostly training with the Army, but it had not been a place he had felt at home. In fact, during his time with the Army Corp of Engineers he had spent most of his time in the deserts of Africa, engineering irrigation solutions for small remote areas. The forest though familiar was not the comfort he had hoped it would be.

He continued to sit for a moment, not trusting his muscles to stand, he missed the desert, missed the work, he had been good at it, in fact it had been his reputation of solving unsolvable problems that had brought him to the attention of the ARC project.

Marcus shook his head as memories flooded his mind, the machine found in the ice, the discovery of its purpose as a weapon and then the panic.

The ARC project had been formed as a last-ditch effort, they had studied the machine, learned from it and then applied some of that technology to allow mankind the ability to launch into space and sleep away centuries as it waited for the planet to heal.

“Here I am” he said, again uttering that gravelly voice which was damn near unrecognizable to him. He shook it off as he unsteadily got to his feet. Shuffling over to the ship he leaned down and studied the damage to the hull it isn’t going to fly again he thought walking around the small vessel, the pod that had returned him to the planet and for a moment he looked up, he imagined for a moment he could see the large mothership that hovered in geosynchronous orbit, pods lined up in there docks as they waited for the Artificial Intelligence to deem the planet safe and begin launch sequence.

He had spent centuries on board that ship, sleeping, frozen, just waiting for the computer to finally launch him and all his fellow volunteers back to the planet that had birthed humanity. Turning with a start as something large moved through the woods some distance away, he felt fear creep up his back and shambled his way towards the rear of the teardrop shaped ship.

He might have been trained as a soldier, but Marcus Gavin had spent his career building and creating, not fighting what few combat skills he had were remnants of the training he had once received in Basic training.

Reaching the back of the small vessel he breathed a sigh a relief to see that the rear section had been undamaged. He listened for another tell-tale sign of the large creature in the woods, but none came, feeling around the surface of the vessel he found the small indent he had been looking for and pushed, a recessed keyboard slid smoothly from the ship, tapping in a code, he waited for what seemed like an eternity as a door slid open, revealing a packed storage compartment.

Marcus began pulling out the gear stored there, mostly emergency supplies should he find himself far from civilization, a backpack, a tent, food and stored water all of which he stacked neatly next to the ship.

Reaching into the rear of the compartment Marcus smiled as his hand closed over a large black plastic case. Sliding it out, it opened it to reveal a Military issue carbine and pistol, complete with extra clips stored neatly in the padded case.

Plucking the rifle, a magazine and a handful of rounds from the case he quickly pushed a few rounds into the clip and slapped it home, pulling back the charging handle he felt it slam home with a reassuring clank, the metal-on-metal sound of a bullet being chambered comforting as he moved around the ship facing the direction of the sound.

After some deliberation, he pointed the rifle at a large tree and aimed, squeezing the trigger to let loose a warning shot. Depressing the trigger, he tensed for the recoil of the small bullpup and was rewarded with a hollow click. Marcus pulled his cheek from the stock, studying the weapon curiously he ejected the round and chambered another, squeezing the trigger, once again came the metallic click. “What the hell” he whispered looking at the weapon. His voice sounding at least semi normal he thought distractedly.

Pulling the magazine, he popped a round out of the magazine and proceeded to rummage around in the overloaded pack until he came out with a small tool case. Carefully he removed the round from the shell and upending the metal casing, after a few hard taps a small solid clump of yellowish rock tumbled out of the bullet casing. “Of all the stupid…” He began, closing his eyes to swallow down the panic starting to build in his chest, expired he thought wanting to either laugh or cry, he wasn’t sure which, apparently no one had sufficiently solved the problem of bullets a few centuries old he marveled.

Staring at the useless solidified cordite powder in his hand, he simply shook his head, the guns were useless he realized, returning the carbine to the black case he began searching the equipment for anything else he could use. Within twenty minutes he had laid out an Ontario K-Bar knife and a survival hatchet.

Shaking his head, he picked up the knife and weighed it in his hand if it’s as big as it sounds, this is just going to piss it off, he thought but hell its better than nothing.

He had spent his entire military career being a creator, a problem solver not a killer, not a destroyer he thought. Which is why at the young age of twenty-seven he had already developed a reputation in both the Army and the private sector as the go to person when an engineering problem had been too daunting or unsolvable, He had always managed to find a solution and implement it much to the amazement of his superiors and his peers. The young man scanned the surrounding trees and after a moment picked up the hatchet and with a few sure strikes came away with a long straight branch, scanning the surrounding forest floor he quickly took the edge of the hatchet over the staff, sharpening the edge, after a few minutes he ran a finger over his handywork, happy with the sharpened point he leaned the staff against a tree, but still within reach as he took care of his next problem.

Stripping out of the wet chemical covered one piece outfit he rummaged through one of the cases until he produced a set of military battle dress, socks a few t-shirts and some fresh underwear, he worked slowly, doing his best to wipe away the chemicals that covered his body head to toe, the mixture that had assisted in his cryogenic sleep now merely an annoyance, much like the birth fluid on a newborn he thought, running one of the spare t-shirts through his hair to remove as much of the sticky substance as possible, he dressed wincing at the way the clothing caught on his still sticky skin he found himself feeling better.

Marcus stood there taking an appreciative breath of the clean forest air, he had heard the potential devastation the weapon would have wrought, hell he could have returned to a desert, or worse a planet barren of all life, he was pleased to see the surrounding woods untouched by what they thought would be the end of the planet.

The machine was ancient when they pulled it from the ice of the arctic it was a mystery, for fifty years it sat dormant at a research facility, the scientists in charge of studying it had not known what it was they had, then during an experiment the machine had suddenly activated. It had taken another year to finally figure out what it was that they had turned on, more importantly how to read the countdown that had begun on that fateful day.

In their efforts they had lost a year out of six, leaving five years before the machine would destroy mankind, releasing virulent pathogens and nanite armies to remove humans and their creations.

Shortly thereafter the ARC project was started, taking technology learned from the machine, they began to build ships, technologies and the process of placing humans in Cryonic sleep, freezing them until such time that they would return.

There should be more, more pods, more people he thought, looking around and seeing no sign of another pod or human. He needed information he thought reaching into the pod and from the center of the control system removed a metallic object that looked like a chrome egg, another piece of that altered technology he thought, placing the small device on the ground, it began to pulse red. Standing and watching it, he waited as the red lights turned yellow and then a solid green, once it had made its connection with the mothership above, the small egg began to rise off of the ground, coming to float at eye level, as Marcus watched a person began to form around the device first as a wireframe and then filling out as the holographic projectors within activated, eventually leaving a dark silver silhouette of a person standing in front of him. “Sentinel is online Marcus Gavin, by your command” the soft female voice stated and he sighed, at least the VI worked he thought, it was a simple virtual interface, without an intelligence of its own, the device would connect to the ship, allowing the Artificial intelligence there to interact with a human, thus like a puppet for the AI, it would give him an interface to communicate with the ship and hopefully other volunteers he thought.

“Sentinel, please review mission and bring me up to speed on the current situation” he stated clearly, as he watched the silhouette froze for a minute, the device communicating and receiving information from the ship, the distance to the ship still circling the earth causing a small-time lag. Finally, the VI nodded its head “Certainly Marcus” it began, and the image of the person vanished, forming instead into an image of the planet hanging in front of him. He knew it was from the ship’s archives, the image centuries old, from when the mission began but still seeing Earth and all its lights and people from space caused his breath to pause, it was his home he thought, watching as the planet lazily spun in front of him.

“Beginning time lapse of events” Sentinel Stated and after a moment the earth’s rotation began to speed up as the AI sped up the recorded image of the planet and as Marcus watched, ships launched from the surface and quickly began to load into the mothership, that had been the pods, they had loaded everyone into them on earth and then like cargo shipped the frozen volunteers to the mothership, loading them into the berths.

The flurry of activity stopped, and the earth continued to spin, the rotation speeding up even more as the AI accelerated the view even more.

Then to Marcus’s horror the lights on the planet began to go out, slow at first and then faster and faster, before long the planet was dark, a red mist began to crawl over the surface, reminding Marcus of a colony of ants as each continent disappeared, the planet covered in a red haze, he didn’t know what it was but decided to wait to ask, instead allowing the visual briefing to continue, eventually the red haze faded as the planet spun, faster and faster.

For almost thirty minutes Marcus stared in rapt fascination as the the planet spin at incredible speeds, the surface a blue blur until instantly it slowed and as Marcus watched, pods exploded from the mothership and began to descend to earth, as he watched a second and then a third mothership came into view and those two launched its pods, the small metal ships descending to earth, then the planet sped up again, slowing once in a while as a random pod launched, then it would speed up again repeating the process a little time later, this happened twelve times, until a final pod launched, descending to earth and the visual briefing stopped.

Marcus stood there silent as he thought through what he just witnessed, something is wrong, he thought with alarm, playing it back in his head. “Sentinel, what can you tell me about the red dust that was released over the planet” he said and waited as the earth dissolved and yet again and the human representation reappeared in front of him.

“From our sensors, it was a swarm of nanite machines, its purpose was to deconstruct any artificial material on the planet, once done the swarm eventually died, however our scans indicate as they cleared the planet, they left large crystal formations covering the planet, these formations then began to pulse with a frequency that has since interfered with our ability to document and record from the planet surface.

Again, Marcus paused, looking around he finally noticed small crystal growths on the trees and ground, the red, blue and green crystal spires seeming to grow on anything. He stepped over and bent down to study a spire, It looked harmless he thought and reaching out, touched it with his finger, just as quickly he pulled it away, as if the rock had bit him, slowly Marcus reached out again and touched the rock, it thrummed as if power was coursing through the small rock, he could feel the vibration into his fingers and hand, After a moment he pulled his hand away, as he tried to count how many crystals he could see, Marcus quickly lost count at a thousand, almost every tree had at least one he thought, such an invasive species and shaking his head he turned back to the VI “Are the crystals some kind of generator or communication equipment?” he asked and again the VI paused as it communicated with the AI on his mothership.

“Yes to both questions, there is a sort of power emanating through them but the source is unknown and they are operating on a wavelength, sending out a low level communications, though it is too low to reach orbit and only seems effective up to a thousand feet from the crystal itself, the signal is constant so it is more of a simple hum then anything intelligent, also you will notice the crystals are no longer giant spire, after a few centuries time has broken them down, what is left is on the plants and in the soil, becoming part of the ecosystem, the crystals seem to be benign and coexist with the environment” Sentinel finished.

Marcus shook his head again looking back to the crystal, that was an interesting mystery, but one outside of his expertise he thought. “Sentinel why launch random pods after the initial exodus?” he asked, remembering the lone pods launched over time. He waited for a response.

“Due to a malfunction, over thirty pods remained on the ship, as they were repaired, they were then launched and returned to earth, as of this time twelve of the thirty have been returned over a period of three centuries” the VI finished and Marcus shook his head not believing what he had just heard

“Sentinel, what is the reason for the timeframe, surely it has not taken that long to fix twelve pods?” he asked, something wasn’t right, but this was a machine, not made to be malicious or nefarious he reassured himself.

The VI paused, this time longer than normal when it came back the silhouette shrugged in a very human manner that caused Marcus to almost take a step back at the action.

“That is unknown, the answer to that question is not available beyond administration level access” Sentinel stated, and Marcus narrowed his eyes, since when did a repair get top level access only, he wondered.

“Sentinel, who authorized the change in security for the repair information?” he asked and again waited for the machine’s answer “That information is not available beyond administration level access” the machine stated. Marcus shook his head, something about that wasn’t right but he had much more pressing issues, he mentally prepared himself and then asked the question.

“Sentinel, I assume the last pod to return was mine, what is the timeframe from the original exodus to my pod returning to the planet” he asked, but he had seen the briefing and new well he wouldn’t like the answer.

After a moment Sentinel came back “Two hundred twelve years since exodus” she said, and it felt as if he had been kicked in the gut as the breath left his lungs, placing his hands on the knees he tried to get control of the looming panic that threatened to overtake him. Two hundred years, people have been on the planet for two centuries he thought, what the hell happened. More importantly, where is everyone, why had no one come to welcome him he wondered, thinking through his options he nodded to himself and queried Sentinel again.

“Sentinel, can you scan the surrounding area for populations, civilization or communication of any kind, purpose is to find a concentration of people” he finished and waited with bated breath as the VI paused, communication with the ship and gathering those results.

Sentinel returned quicker than he expected “Marcus because of the interference, I am unable to lock on any location of a human population, however I can tell you that there are no communications either over this location or the entire North American continent, no digital or analog broadcasts have been detected since the exodus itself” Sentinel stated, again causing Marcus to pause in an alarmed panic as the small ember of hope died in his chest.

How can that be he thought, people have been back for two hundred years, with the supplies and expertise of the twenty thousand people returned, surely there would be some sort of civilization he thought, again he closed his eyes, the weight of the information threatening to crush him as he battled to keep the panic at bay. Were there still people left? he wondered, could the effects of the machine have lasted causing those that returned to have died his mind continued.

That’s not helpful he chastised himself beginning to pace, he needed a plan, he couldn’t stay out here in the woods waiting for someone to come and get him. He was no survivalist, he was a damn engineer, aside from basic classes he had no real ability to survive in the woods for long periods of time he thought, suddenly thinking maybe he should have gone to ranger school when he had the change.

After a few minutes of pacing he had not come up with anything that could even be considered a plan. With a sigh he turned back to the VI “Sentinel, based on the current information do you have a suggestion for a course of action that will allow me to learn the disposition and possibly reconnect with the population on the planet” he asked and with a mental wince, waited for the answer.

A moment later the VI nodded “Marcus, based on the limited information we have it is my suggestion that the first place to stop would be the supply bunkers, you have limited supplies and since it could some time to locate others, you will need to ensure your ability to survive” The VI stated calmly and Marcus could have slapped himself on the forehead.

“Of Course” He mumbled “The damn bunkers”, during the planning phase of the project, the ARC leaders had set about building bunkers throughout the western united states, where the volunteers would later land to rebuild, knowing the ships couldn’t carry the supplies and the status of the planet would be unknown, bunkers were created to ensure that the equipment, supplies and food would be available to the volunteers upon their return.

Marcus knew it was a long shot, he was ten centuries late to the party, it was very possible that those bunkers would be empty, but maybe there would be a clue as to where the volunteers had done. Either way he thought, it was a good idea “Sentinel, prepare to guide me to the closest bunker” Marcus commanded and began to collect his supplies.

As the sun began to descend over the canopy, bringing dusk to the forest, Marcus dropped the pack with a grunt, Sentinel walked over to the tree, standing there and waiting for orders, as he collapsed upon the pack and eyed the VI, he knew it didn’t really walk, the device simply floating as it gave the appearance its hologram was walking with him. For the entire day he had followed the damn VI as they navigated the forest westward towards the closest bunker to his ships landing site.

He had covered the ship with dead branches, doing his best to hide it, he wasn’t sure from what or whom, but it seemed like a good idea at the time he thought, but the exertion of doing that on top of walking made him rethink his earlier decision.

“Sentinel, when will we reach the bunker” he asked, playing his own little game of ‘are we there yet’ with the machine.

“We will reach the bunker tomorrow at noon based on our days progress” Sentinel stated and with a grunt, Marcus nodded as he began to remove the tent and set it up, after clumsily setting up his camp and finally getting a fire started, he was heating a small can of freeze dried corn beef hash, using some of the precious bottled water to reconstitute the food, the result looking more like vomit then food he thought, a rustling from the trees caught his attention. Standing he pulled the hatchet and scanned the canopy as more branches shivered with movement.

Something was up there he thought taking a step back, never taking his eyes off the tree.

He almost jumped out of his skin when a black tendril broke free of the densely covered branch and took off across the expanse towards another tree, stopping halfway and simply hovering as it waited for something.

Marcus stood there, his jaw agape and the hatchet forgotten as he studied the creature, now fully displayed in the waning sunlight of the day.

“Sentinel, can you scan that creature” he whispered and waited as the VI put its palm up, virtual windows appearing into existence as the device began to scan the area leaving Marcus to study it.

It is a snake he thought, following the black scaly body, which measured about six feet in length, ending at a narrow snake’s head, that wasn’t what bothered him he reflected, his eyes now focusing on the bat like wings sprouting from halfway along its body, the membranous wings lazily flapping as they cupped the air, keeping the animal in the air. “What the hell” he breathed, not able to take his eyes from the creature.

“Marcus, it appears to be some kind of hybrid animal, it is not the only one as others of its kind are close by, I would say from the number that this is not a fluke but a mutation in the animal, one that has evolved to become the species” Sentinel stated, loud enough to startle the creature and send it flying into the far tree line, just as quickly about ten more erupted from the first tree and joined it, the flock moving at a fast speed to join its compatriot. “Well it seems some things have changed since my last time here” he said half astonished and half smiling at his weak joke.

The next day as the sun finished its climb to mid-day Marcus found himself standing at the base of a large hill, the churned earth having settled long ago from the looks of it

“Where are we Sentinel?” he asked looking around, searching for signs of the large warehouse like bunker that should be here. For a few moments the VI stood stalwart before moving again towards the large mound of dirt. “The bunker is directly in front of us based on the coordinates in the system, however all scans show that it has been removed from beneath the earth, possibly by the same nanite infestation that removed all artificial material on the planet” she said floating up the berm, Marcus scrambled to follow. Shaking his head, he struggled to climb the simple slope a headache that had plagued him all morning getting worse, a hum had started early that morning and the more they had walked the worse it had gotten, here at the base of the hill it almost felt as if his entire cranium were vibrating, as if he were following a sound and it had begun to get worse. Making it to the top he stood there looking over the expanse and marveled at the large hole filled to the brim with crystal spires, all colors and all sizes, the spires reaching from the deep pit towards the sky, as if someone had lined the entire thing with spikes to kill a giant he thought staring in disbelief at the sheer amount of the rocks, the nanites had converted, the supplies hell the bunker itself into damn crystals he thought, staring at the impossibility of what had become of the large structure.

“This is not possible, according to my coordinates this is the location of the closest bunker Marcus” Sentinel stated, her palm outstretched as she began gathering readings from the enormous collection of crystals. He didn’t need the scans to know what had happened, it was obvious he thought.

He slumped on the edge in defeat, rubbing his head as the thrumming grew worse, what the hell is that? he wondered squinting from the pain down into the large hole of colorful rocks. After a moment he slid down the side of the hill and walked a small distance from the crater sized hole, the further he was from the collection of crystals the quieter his head became.

Finally once he had reached a distance where he could begin to think Marcus began to pace, he was a problem solver, his abilities relied in recognizing patterns others missed and something in the back of his mind was going off, was it something that sentinel had said that morning he wondered, continuing to wear a track in the forest floor as he concentrated on what he had learned from the machine over the past few days.

There was something there about the crystals and power, something about a signal, that might explain the feeling in his head, was it possible that he could sense the power or the signal, similar to some who were able to sense powerlines the closer they came to them he wondered.

He was side tracking himself and knew it, that wasn’t what was bothering him. Finally pausing in mid pace, he turned to the VI image “Sentinel, didn’t you say that the crystals appeared after the dissipation of the red nanite swarm?” he asked, knowing there was a correlation there, pulling on the thread of thought, he tried to follow it to its conclusion.

After a moment pause the VI returned “Yes Marcus, why do you ask?” it queried, with a simple nod he continued to pace, confirming his initial theory.

“Sentinel, scan the makeup of the crystals in that crater and then match it to the known chemical components of what would have been in that bunker” Marcus stated, crossing his fingers that he was wrong. It took almost fifteen minutes before the VI returned “It was not easy, the crystals themselves making remote scanning next to impossible, but this unit was able to collect enough local data to do an extrapolation” it began as Marcus waited impatiently for his answer.

“According to the scan, the chemical makeup of the crystal collection matches that of the makeup of the building and supplies within the bunker at eighty seven percent” Sentinel finished and waited for Marcus’s next command.

Blowing out a breath he eyed the trees around him seeing the crystal growths, and finally knowing what he was looking at, what those beautiful monoliths represented. “Sentinel, I think we are looking at what was left of the human race, I think we are seeing what happened to the components of every building, monument, food wrapper and who knows what else that the swarm destroyed, I think these crystals are the tombstone to our race” he finished still eyeing the crystals. Sentinel did not respond, simple stood there waiting for the next order, despite the epiphany that Marcus had just laid on them both.

Suddenly he felt tired, drained of whatever energy remained in him, sitting down he hung his head, thinking of all that had been taken from this world, taken from him as he continued to stare at the innocent looking crystal. As he sat there, a movement caught his eye, looking to his left he watched as a small amount of crystal spires began to move through the forest floor, he couldn’t believe it, was it possible that the crystals themselves were alive he wondered, slowing getting up and watching as the mound continued to move. He crept over, slowly as the mound moved once again, making his way over, Marcus peered down into the semi tall grass and began to laugh, under the mound of crystals rose a very familiar site, the heard of a turtle rising from beneath the ornate shell. “That’s a lot of bling my friend” he laughed shaking his head. The turtle did not seem impressed with his observation and continued to move towards the safety of the trees as Marcus continued to study the crystal shell.

“Sentinel” he called and the VI walked over to stand next to him “Can you scan this, is this shell covered with crystal growths?” he asked, and Sentinel stooped down, running its hand over the shell as new windows appeared in midair, listing information and graphs, the data being transmitted to the ship, analyzed and then returned. Sentinel stood and turned to Marcus “It appears that the shell is crystal Marcus, after a quick scan it appears that this creature’s DNA has been altered as was the snakes” it stated.

That alone wiped the smile from his face, Were the crystals somehow changing the animal life on the planet he wondered, then recalled the changes to his own body that the ARC project had propagated in order to allow him and all. The volunteers to survive cryogenic sleep, changes that been sampled from biological compounds found within the machine itself.

With another swell of fear forming he turned to the VI “Sentinel, scan me and tell me *if the alterations that were completed at ARC have any similarity to the changes happening to the animals on Earth” he said, praying to anyone that would listen to ensure he was wrong in his assumption. After a few minutes Sentinel spoke “There are some similarities to the changes that were made to your own DNA, but they are rudimentary at best in matching it to the fauna on this planet, when taken into account the vast differences in the DNA you have requested an analysis of” it stated and Marcus almost breathed a sigh of relief, pausing as a thought shot through his mind causing him to wince

“Sentinel, extrapolate for changes over time and tell me how similar the changes would be to say this turtle a few centuries from now” he said and again waited, hoping he was wrong.

Sentinel returned after a time “Good assumption Marcus, the changes to your own DNA bear very similar markers to ones that theoretically will occur over most of the animal population of the planet in four centuries but again, the exact nature of the changes cannot be determined because there is no one to one comparison” Sentinel finished and Marcus winced again, somehow whatever changes the ARC project had given him with the advanced DNA manipulation were some kind of blue print to whatever would happen to the animals here.

That brought up a few unpleasant thoughts he reflected “Sentinel, based on the information you have at the time communications were cut off from Earth, did they surmise a function for the machine?” he asked. Thinking he knew what they would have found. “Yes Marcus, according to the. Records, the final theory prior to communications being cut was that the device was not a weapon at all, but an advanced tera former” she finished.

Whatever had built the damn thing thought Marcus had set it upon his planet to ensure that it would eventually be habitable for their form of life, why so long he wondered, surely with the technology that he had seen, the machine. Could have simply altered the planet and the species, why go through slow changes he wondered. He had a few theories but nothing he could prove, besides he had more important problems he thought.

Marcus setup camp once again, but instead of settling in, he began pacing, he had to find people, had to find out what happened to the original volunteers, had they succeeded and was there a civilization for him to return to, or had they simply died off, leaving Marcus the sole heir to humanity. He wondered.

He paced most of the afternoon, he needed a plan, with limited supplies he had to forage, had to find people if they existed, he needed to get the motherships sensors working, without the ability to scan the planet for life, he could wander forever trying to find people, but the more he thought about it the more frustrated he became, he was a mechanical engineer, not a damn software engineer, if there was a problem that required the sensors to be calibrated, he wasn’t the man to do it, he admitted slumping down in defeat next to the tent.

As the sun settled behind the horizon, the autumn air bit at his skin as the temperature began to drop. Lighting a fire, he huddled next to it sulking in his thoughts, He had failed, there was no way to use the ship to locate humans he thought, he would be forced to wander aimlessly hoping to run into a village or city he thought, pulling out a can, he rotated it to find a general label for beef stew.

Sitting alone he grew deeper into depression at the thought of those few people now long dead, centuries ago and yet here he sat, alone and eating.

He lay leaning against a tree, the final embers of the firelight casting shadows across the ground and tent as if a kabuki show were in progress for his entertainment. Closing his eyes he breathed out, his body and mind were still recovering from the frozen centuries of sleep but yet he had to push himself, had to find others, his limited supplies meant that sooner or later he would have to find a way to feed himself out here or find a town or people to aid him. Marcus did his best to concentrate on the task at hand, pushing back the fear and doubt that threatened to take over his conscious thought, the small whispers that taunted him every moment of waking thought what if he were the last, what if everyone else was dead, what if he would simply wander the woods until he died, alone and forgotten. He had been lost fighting against those very thoughts when something shot across the canopy above him, moving from branch to branch and catching his attention.

With a light groan he lifted himself from the tree as his joints protested the interruption from there rest. Studying the canopy above he caught another movement, this one punctuated with light as it flitted between the branches, his sore joints were soon forgotten as he continued to follow the strange lights, sometimes alone and other times grouped in three or four.

“What the hell are you?” he whispered, trying to get a look at what could be making the odd lights, perhaps another animal that was in the midst of being altered by the mysterious machine, that even now, all these centuries later was effecting the planet.

He stood there for nearly an hour doing his best to catch a glimpse of the lights, but the distance made it nearly impossible for Marcus to see the source of the strange lights.

A snapping of a twig near the base of a tree caught his attention and he whipped his head in that direction, for a moment he tensed, ready to run should the sound be caused by a large predator, but he quickly relaxed when he caught sight of the small white furred monkey standing there at the tree’s base, its head was cocked as it studied him, the little creature more curious then scared.

“Hey little guy, what are you doing here?” he asked. Wondering how the hell a monkey was wild in the western America’s. He was no animal expert, but this looked like the spider monkeys he had seen on the various animal planet episodes he had so loved to watch.

Marcus didn’t move, didn’t try to get closer and did his best to remain neutral and not a threat to the much smaller animal. After a short time, he figured that he had done a good job as the monkey turned to the tree, dismissing him.

As Marcus watched, the little monkey walked over grabbing two of the crystal spires and to his astonishment the simian’s fur began to glow, it seemed to draw power from the crystal, in fact if Marcus cleared his mind, he could almost hear the thrumming of the spire as the monkey continued to touch it.

The little spider monkey grew brighter and brighter the longer he held onto the crystals, after a time it released its grip, turning for a last look at the lone human, the small simian chirped a goodbye and launched itself up into the tree, soaring from branch to branch to join its fellow compatriots far above.

“You don’t see that every day” Marcus said shaking his head. What other animals will I find on this trip he wondered continuing to watch the monkeys frolic above him.

Eventually the exhaustion got the better of him and he retired to the tent. He lay there as sleep was a long time coming, he remembered the feeling he had gotten when getting close to what was left of the bunker, “I wonder” he said and closed his eyes, clearing his head he listened both with his mind and his ears, for a long time nothing came but as time went by he began to feel or hear, he couldn’t really tell a distant vibration, then another and yet another after that.

Is that the crystals he wondered, were they putting off a sound or was he sensing the power coursing through them. No matter how he tried he couldn’t tell whether it was a sound or if it was something more mental. Eventually sleep took him, the thrumming of crystals and the strange creatures of the earth were forgotten as he slipped deep into unconsciousness.

“Where are you fallen, where did your vessel come down?” came a voice, Marcus looked around but saw nothing but black, there was no light, no feeling as he seemed to float in an ethereal space, for a moment he thought the voice itself was his imagination when the disembodied voice came again, seeming to echo through his mind.

“Tell me where you are fallen, let me come to you, let me help you” came the voice again, Marcus could not feel ground beneath him, moving his hand to his face he could not see it, he felt it when his palm encountered his nose, but with the absence of light he couldn’t even see his hand inches from him. “Hello?” he called, the words seeming flat, a vast contrast to the echoing of the alien voice. He waited but no answer came so he called out again “Hey, who are you?” again his voice flat.

“Where are you fallen, call out to me, use your gift and tell me where you are” the voice came again. Marcus began to feel panic take over his thoughts as he tried to move, tried to see. His mouth opened to scream out, to call out. He shot up with a start the scream escaping from his lips as his head hit the top of the tent, opening his eyes the light of morning played with the shadows of branches off the fabric as the scream died a stillbirth in his throat.

“A dream” he said, a smile of relief spreading over his face as he lay back down, allowing his body to calm and his heart to stop racing. “What the fuck” he breathed shaking his head at his own hysterics. “You have enough issues without freaking out Marc” he said to himself, after a time he calmed down, dressing he crawled out of the tent to the cold morning sun.

Surveying the forest, he studied the large old oaks and poplars, the forest going on for miles, most of the leaves had fallen from the trees, but there was still enough on the branches to give the forest color.

Crossing his arms, he braced himself as a light breeze played across the forest. It was a short time later as a fire roared warming him and breakfast had long since finished when the epiphany came. Sitting there he still had no answer on how to find civilization when suddenly the simplest solution popped into his head. “You idiot” he said shaking his head as he scrambled over to the pack and dug out the egg. He had since turned off Sentinel after the bunker disappointment, but now needed her access to the ship.

Smiling he watched as the little egg pulsed red, then yellow and finally green. The computer rendered figure appeared, Marcus didn’t wait for Sentinel to give its familiar greeting. “Sentinel does the ship still have access to long range camera’s?” he asked and waited impatiently for the answer.

For the first time since waking Marcus was excited, I hope this works he thought as he willed the machine to speed up, to answer his request, the action was impudent, but made him feel a little better. The VI moved “Marcus, we still have full functionality over seventy percent of our available cameras to utilize in analyzing land masses, weather and other events on the planet” Sentinel stated.

“What kind of information can we gain on the landscape, more importantly how is your ability to extrapolate a geometric analysis from real-time photos of the land?” Marcus asked and he thought he could see a spark of interest in the VI’s eyes.

Could it be it was a bit more than a simple interface he wondered or was he merely anthropomorphizing the computer in a desperate attempt to develop a connection with another person.

He would need to watch that he thought, it would be too easy to fall into the thought process that Sentinel was a flesh and blood creature, well an emotional sentient being at the very least he corrected, looking at the silver outline of the female frame.

“That ability it available to us Marcus, by your command” Sentinel finished, waiting for the command that would set the computer into action. Taking a pause, he ordered his thoughts, he knew what he wanted but now he had to ensure he said it in such a way the computer did as well.

“Sentinel, I want you to comb the landscape, look for straight lines or other formations, tree removal or paths that are too symmetrical to be natural occurrences, once found, analyze the probability of them being a human creation, then center the cameras upon the area and scan for signs of buildings or construction, checking the landscape for fields of a single plant or humans themselves within that area” he finished, waiting with bated breath as Sentinel passed the information to the ship pausing once again for a response.

It seemed an agonizingly long time before the VI began to move once more. “We are more than capable of doing that, however because of the age and condition of the hardware, it will have to be done carefully, this process will take, at the very least the remainder of the day Marcus” Sentinel finished and then waited for Marcus to decide.

To him it was not even a decision “Sentinel, proceed with the analysis, please contact me the second we can confirm any sign of human existence” he finished, releasing a breath, finally he thought a plan that just might work.

Turning he concentrated on the woods, from this elevation he could scan the forest as the canopy stretched for miles in all directions without a break or end in sight.

This might become my reality he thought still staring at the sea of green and could imagine it covering the entire planet. There was still a possibility that the ARC volunteers who had come two centuries ago had run into problems, war or the inability to reproduce and aside from those few still aboard the ship, he would find himself all alone, the single survivor, the monument to his once prolific race and in the back of his mind, those whispers began to ebb in on his conscious thoughts, telling him he was alone, he was the last of humanity, closing his eyes Marcus fought them back, returning them to the depths of his mind.

Not for the first time the thought of ending his life, of putting himself out of the misery of a lonely existence devoid of any human contact reared its ugly head, the thought disturbed him less than the fact that it was no longer horrifying, in fact it was almost welcome he thought and shuddered, pushing it to the back of his mind with the chorus of voices.

Closing his eyes Marcus cleared his mind trying to silence the voices, in doing so he felt the familiar thrum again, he could feel the light touch of the crystals against his mind, as if he and the spires shared a connection.

It was possible he thought remembering the shortcuts and rushed engineering the scientists had done on material and technology they had managed to harvest from the machine, finding a way to fuse it into a human they had come up with the revolutionary breakthrough that would allow the volunteers to survive and be revived once put into the frozen death that was cryo-stasis.

There had been quite a lot of discussion and arguments between the research scientists. He was no biologist but introducing an unknown alien material that had an amazing ability to adapt itself to the host despite the lack of research and testing on it, didn’t sound like a good scientific practice.

Bringing his attention back to the immediate surroundings he studied the incredibly large trunks spotted with the colorful crystals, he knew the forest was old, not just a few years but potentially centuries old from the size and width of the large trunks surrounding him, some of the older trees could fit a car within them.

He had never even seen anything this large on TV much less in person, most of the forests during his time had been clear cut and replaced more than once for things like paper products he mused, stepping closer to the largest of one such OAK, its trunk nearly fifty feet across, the bark, old and gnarled from ages of weathering the rain and cold.

After removing humans and all that they had created, the machine had left the animals and the flora, as if simply resetting the planet, removing the most intelligent race housed there.

“You were right to think it was terraforming, but the real question was, for whom, are they dead or merely waiting” he said to the tree, running his fingers over the old bark. His hand falling to one of the crystal spires growing out of the trunk, dropping his hand he regarded the simple rock.

This he thought is all that is left of everything we built, deconstructed, the elements used to create crystals that are somehow powered and putting out a signal that I am able to receive, what could be the purpose of these things, the machine went to great lengths to both create them and then seed them over the planet.

He didn’t think he would ever know, it had completed its work centuries ago and for all he knew it was now rusted and buried at the bottom of the ocean, its creators long dead and humanity the last victim to an old program from a derelict long past its purpose.

Marcus shook it off, he didn’t have time to be morose, there was very little purpose in figuring out any of this he thought as he began to pace the small clearing.

Something was happening to him, his mind was changing, he could feel it, he didn’t like to admit it but it was beginning to bother him, every day that passed his ability to sense crystals, the currents of energy that they emanated was growing, what else was happening that he didn’t know about he wondered, watching as a flock of the flying snakes broke from a tree, descending on a small group of large flying bugs, they soared and dipped in the predatory dance, sweeping up the flying delicious morsels and then moving to another tree to conceal themselves until the next group came by.

The complete absurdity of flying snakes was almost enough to pull Marcus from his train of thought. Closing his eyes, he cleared his mind, again feeling the vibration of crystals, he could almost see them through his closed lids, they had sung to him in his mind, the tone almost pleasant he thought, shaking his head he opened his eyes and turned to regard Sentinel, still standing completely still, she waited on the data from the ship. Using a tree to rest his back, he settled in for the same wait as he watched the sun play through the few leaves above. The day was cold, but tolerable as he closed his eyes enjoying the small warmth of the sun on his face.

The sounds of water slamming against rock emanated from below as Marcus surveyed the black costal rocks, he suddenly found himself in front of. “What the hell” he whispered looking out over the black ocean, the broad whitecaps barely visible in the moonlight as he let his eyes roam to the horizon.

“There you are fallen one, I thought you had hidden yourself from me” came a voice from behind him, turning he found a young blonde woman standing not far behind him, her storm blue eyes lit over his face as a broad smile broke the contour of her alabaster features.

He turned to stand in front of the woman, eyeing her as the continued sound of the waves slammed against the shore far below, the ocean spray rising up over the edge of the cliff.

“Who are you and where the hell are, we?” Marcus asked the tone severe to hide the fear he felt, how the hell did I get here he wondered, looking up and down the coast, nothing here was recognizable to him, he had been in the woods.

It had been mid-day he thought, did someone drug him or had he somehow been transported here, he couldn’t recall any technology that would do that, but his world had ended centuries ago, who knew what wonders existed in a world with flying snakes he reflected. This was the first sign of a human he had seen he realized, why was he so apprehensive he wondered, the hairs on the back of his neck rising as the woman approached.

Something about her scared the hell out of him, though he could not put his finger on it. The realization caused him to take an involuntary step back as she approached. This did not go unnoticed and she stopped advancing, her hands going out to her sides to show they were empty.

“I mean you no harm fallen one, I merely wish to find you, we have a common enemy, one who ended our world, though more yours then mine” she said, her hand coming up to point out towards the water and Marcus turned, following the finger towards the horizon, then he heard it, a low thrumming, a pulse as if someone were beating a very large drum, it took him a moment to realize he felt it more than heard it, in his head and he turned back to the woman, as he did his eyes took in the details he had missed. The crushed red velvet dress and the wrists and neck covered in jewelry, not garish, subtle but expensive he thought cocking his head and standing his ground despite his mind’s insistence that he run from this place, this person. “What is that?” he asked instead, curiosity getting the better of him.

The woman’s smile fell from her face as their eyes locked “It is the engine of old fallen one, the same machine that killed the ancients, it returns” she simply said and Marcus wanted to ask what, how did she know this, where was it but the scene faded, the woman and the scenery going to black. “Marcus” came a voice from within his mind.

His eyes opened and instantly seared with the light of day “What the hell” he grumbled, his eyes adjusting once again to the day. “Where was I?” he asked coming to and seeing the VI standing there moving again. “I don’t understand” she said cocking her head in a very human gesture.

“You have not traveled anywhere, you simply dozed off and I woke you” the VI stated, Marcus let his eyes rove over the familiar scene, this is where he had been, was that some kind of dream? He wondered getting to his feet and brushing off the dead leaves that clung to the back of his pants. There had been something familiar about that voice he thought as he recalled the dream from the night before, vision? dream? his mind asking himself, trying to resolve what the hell that had been.

His mind had been altered somehow, he felt the humming of the crystals like some sort of transmission, as if he had suddenly become a radio receiver, could this vision or dream be the same kind of thing he wondered, did this woman have the ability to reach out and communicate with him. If so, it would answer his question of whether humans existed he reflected. Then his mind went to that feeling, something about the woman had scared him, down to his core he thought. As if it hadn’t been a woman but a predator, something that was stalking him, hunting him and his instincts kicked in, trying to save his life.

But in the light of day, in the semi familiar surroundings the feeling had faded quickly, and Marcus couldn’t quite understand what about the woman had frightened him. He still felt on edge, surveying the surrounding he couldn’t shake the feeling of being watched, someone had been in his mind, been within his private world, how could that be and more importantly how the hell did he stop her, he wanted to dismiss it as a dream a simple manifestation of loneliness, but it had felt so real, was it his mind trying desperately to believe he wasn’t alone or was it really some kind of communication.

Taking a breath, he steadied himself, he believed what he had experienced was no dream, no simple figment of his imagination, it had been too real, he had been too present. Closing his eyes he could once again hear the emanations of the crystals, it was almost a pale comparison to the sound he had heard over the horizon, that thrumming he reflected and then recalled the conversation, she had called him fallen one, like she knew he had come from the ship, she knew there were those who came later he surmised, but then she seemed desperate to find out where he was, so she couldn’t track him, nothing she had said to him could have been pulled from his mind he thought.

“She spoke to me” he said, his eyes widening a bit, what were the chances centuries later that this woman would speak an English he could recognize, neutral of all dialects and accents he thought.

The hairs on the back of his neck went up once again, was there a way she had pulled that from his mind he thought, could she read his thoughts, after a few moments of deliberation he hesitantly dismissed it, nothing she had done pointed to it, except for the speech, but that could have been found out he thought, or some mind trick of the communication he thought.

“Sentinel, I take it since you are present and moving, you have information for me” he stated and the VI turned and smiled at him. “I do Marcus, I believe we have found what you are looking for”. He nodded and felt a great weight lift from his chest as he waited for the VI to speak. “It is a bit far, we have extrapolated a location, one that would have been near the original landing site of the main body of volunteers, however over the centuries as the earth has shifted and the machines on board the ARC have become less specific in its coordinates, your landing was not as on target as it should have been” the VI began.

Marcus’s eyes widened what the hell did that mean, could he have landed in the damn ocean had they been off a little more he thought, but decided that was a conversation he didn’t want to have. Turning the VI extended her hand and a map began to build itself in front of them, the area turning so Marcus could get a good look at.

“This is the area the ship felt has the most probability of Humans” she stated as Marcus stepped forward looking over green fields, cut into the woods and followed the clean lines of what appeared to be crops growing in the center of a wooded area, watching the map continued to slowly rotate “stop” he called, taking a quick step towards the hologram and squinting to get a look at something.

“Can you get closer, a better image of the area?” he asked excitedly, the VI paused “I’m sorry, the ship is unable to get any closer, the equipment is centuries old and no longer working up to specifications, this is the best we are able to do” she said and he could hear the regret in her voice, was that programmed in he wondered as his eyes tried to pick out the blurry brown image of what looked like a fence near the edge of the field.

“Better than nothing” Marcus mumbled “Keep looking, we will set out in the morning” he finished and began to set up camp as the VI once again went dormant.

The next morning Marcus awoke to a disappointed looking VI “I’m sorry Marcus, we have found no other signs that we can determine were created by humans, but this is more to the failure of equipment then lack evidence” she interjected, and Marcus nodded. “The ship was only able to search a very small area and its ability to zoom in limited its ability to find evidence of civilization” Sentinel finished.

It would be too good to be true to find a village or city, though if there were humans, and after his ‘dream’ he was absolutely sure there was, the problem still existed, how to reach them. “Sentinel, what is the distance to the established field” he asked and braced himself for the answer. Again, he noticed the sad expression on the face of the VI damn he thought do they program that in to give it a more human appearance, or is that something he was creating, something to connect with the computer that looked similar to a human, he would have to be careful he thought, don’t lose it now Marcus he chided himself, now he was anthropomorphizing the damn VI, he needed to stop. “It is 165 miles to the location we have determined, which will take you about a week and half at your current rate of travel Marcus, however you do not have enough supplies to make the journey, you will have to find a supply of food and within the next few days” the VI stated.

Marcus hung his head, he knew his supplies were getting low, but to hear the VI lay it out he felt panic begin to well up in his stomach, the thought of starving to death, dying in these woods, far from anyone scared him immensely, with a force of will he pushed down on the panic “I am an engineer Sentinel, we will find a way” he said with more conviction then he felt.

For a moment his mind turned to the mysterious woman and the vision, for a moment he thought about trying to reach out, trying to illicit help and then he remembered the feeling she had given him, something about her scared the hell out of him and he was not one to ignore his instincts and dismissed that course of action.

He stood there, his mind heavy with the weight of the long journey ahead as he watched the sun retreat behind the wall of trees and the world grew dark, not long after the nocturnal animals began to wake that the lights of the strange simians began jumping from tree-to-tree Marcus listened as the echo of a screech owl sent its mournful call into the wild. Eventually he retired to the tent, his body tired as it still worked at recovering from his long sleep in space. He was slow, walking at almost an ambling pace, he would need to speed that up despite the pain of his joints and muscles, he would push harder, faster and further he vowed as he drifted off to sleep.

Marcus woke as the sun began to ascend the trees, the early morning light playing across the tent fabric, no visions or dreams had plagued him the prior night allowing him to truly get a decent night’s rest.

Despite the list of problems facing him, he felt better and crawling out of his tent he found Sentinel standing there waiting for him. “Good morning Marcus, after working all night with the ship, I think we have found a route that will give you access to water and minimal terrain to traverse, allowing you not only an easier trip but it might allow you to cut down the time” the VI finished and again Marcus had the impression she was proud of her discovery, had he asked her to do that he thought, trying to remember if he had asked for that kind of help from the VI.

“Why is it you continued working after completing my last request?” he asked eyeing the Hologram suspiciously. The VI didn’t even flinch, simply answered the question devoid of any emotion.

“Due to the issues the solution presented, the ship surmised that additional help was required and proceeded to work through the problem” she said. Marcus continued to eye her “right” he simply said and began to disassemble the tent. Reaching into the pack, his hand brushed against something metal, pulling it out he found a small set of field binoculars, absently he put them in a cargo pocket and closed the pack, in this thick jungle they were useless, but once he managed to get into the clear, those would be invaluable he thought pulling the pack onto his back with a grunt.

“Alright you can take the lead” he said simply still eyeing the VI as he packed everything up, it wasn’t long before he was packed and ready to head out, his joints ached a bit but he felt good, better than he had since landing.

Following the hologram, they walked out of the clearing and back into the thick underbrush of the forest when the loud snapping of a twig off to his left brought him up short. Marcus turned to study the Woodline, remembering the sounds shortly after he had awoken in the forest, how could he have forgotten he thought narrowing his eyes as he tried to see beyond the bushes and trees between him and the sound. “Sentinel, can you scan the area? Are we alone?” he whispered not taking his eyes off of the tree line.

Sentinel stepped forward pushing her palm at the woods, small virtual screens floated to the left and right of her hand, after a few moments Sentinel turned “I’m sorry Marcus, the interference is not allowing for a clean scan of the area, I cannot ascertain what if anything is out there” she finished and just as she completed her answer Marcus caught sight of fur passing between two bushes and the sounds of movement followed right after.

“Sentinel, we are not alone” Marcus whispered, pulling the knife from his belt and taking a step back, he was a damn engineer not special forces, he could build you an entire irrigation system or a house or a bridge with a knife, but killing someone or something, fighting off large predators with a blade, he wasn’t fucking Rambo he thought.

Another branch snapping catching his attention, this one closer, and his heart began to race, adrenaline coursed through his veins, his body going into fight or flight.

“Sentinel, can you sense anything out there?” he asked, knowing the answer before she spoke. “No Marcus, I cannot, but it is obvious we are not alone” she said as something moved at the corner of his vision, snapping his head in the direction he caught the movement of branches but nothing else.

He was being hunted he realized the fear trying to take over, trying to overwhelm his reason as he stood there shaking, his body tense as he waited for whatever it was to show itself. He was in the open and whatever it was, was circling, moving around behind him, he could hear the light shuffling as whatever it was continued to move to his left, a moment later he shook his head “Fuck this” and Marcus bolted in the opposite direction, running as fast as he could, trying to put space between himself and whatever it was hunting him.

Sentinel floated next to him, the little egg that created the hologram able to achieve speeds near thirty miles an hour it easily kept up with Marcus, laden down with gear and puffing out breath after breath as his lungs burned in his chest, he pushed himself harder despite the pain in his joints and muscles.

Suddenly the forest broke and he was once again in the open, his surprise nearly landed him in the river quickly coming up on him. He stopped short, his toes just touching the torrential rapids of the fast-moving river he now found himself staring at.

“Shit” Marcus hissed his head darting around, looking for a way forward or around, his mind searching for a bridge before he realized his mistake. The predator emerged from the woods behind him, and he heard it before turning and finding himself staring face to face with the largest timber wolf he had ever seen, the beast stood nearly five feet, the thing looked practically prehistoric he thought as he studied the intelligent arctic eyes that coldly regarded him with a detached interest, not moving forward nor retreating, the wolf simply stood there, as if it knew he had nowhere to go. Marcus frantically looked around it took him only a few more moments to figure out what the wolf already seemed to know; he was trapped.

It might be large he thought, but it was still only one wolf and he gripped the knife tighter and faced the creature full on, there was still a chance he would live through this he thought, despite the doubt in his head, Marcus moved the knife so the hilt touched his torso, mostly to stop the damn thing from shaking.

A moment later things went from bad to worse as two more wolves moved out on either side of his hunter, these two were smaller, seemingly less disciplined as the largest one, the original wolf chuffed in the direction of its companion, another wolf, also significantly smaller than the first one. Marcus suddenly realized what he was looking at, it was a mother with her cubs, she was teaching them to hunt and Marcus was the prey.

He stepped back, feeling his feet get wet and as he did, mother, as he had decided to refer to it, stepped forward as her ears going flat, a low rumble emanating from her throat as she tensed. This seemed to be a signal he thought as the two smaller grey wolves came to point.

Mother turned to each one chuffing out orders as they began to move out from her location. Marcus eyed them closely watching as the thick muscles moved easily under the mass of dirty grey fur, they might be young and inexperienced, but they were more than capable of taking him on he thought.

The fear almost overtook him and with every ounce of self-control he had he fought it down, trying to keep his head despite the situation. “Come on Marcus, you are a problem solver, now fucking solve this one, before it kills you” his head moving back and forth as the two younger wolves inched further from the mother, circling him as they did. He had seen enough animal planet to know he was completely screwed as he went over the options in his head.

Dismissing each one as he did, then he heard the roar of the rapids behind him, taking a quick look over his shoulder he studied the water for a moment.

“Marcus, I feel obliged to inform you that entering the river gives you a very slim chance of survival, the undertow would most likely kill you” Sentinel stated dispassionately, and Marcus shot her an annoyed look.

“Thanks, any other sage advice for me” he asked and after a moment the VI nodded “The wolves are incapable of seeing my hologram but quite probably can see the machine that displays it, as their eyes are not able to perceive the trick of projection that allows you to visualize a three dimensional person” she finished and then was quiet and Marcus rolled his eyes “Great, at least you will survive” he whispered eyeing the wolves again, they continued to circle, moving closer, he watched as the one on the left stopped and tensed he only had moments before it was on him and with no other options he turned, his legs bending to jump when he felt the weight of the wolf hit his back, nearly spilling him into the river.

The pack and the animals own inexperience saved Marcus, the animal latching onto the backpack, he felt the burning as its hind legs tore into his back and ass I am dead, I am fucking dead Marcus thought, the panic beginning to overwhelm his senses, he had moments before the animal would figure out its mistake and he could hear the hard clap of porcelain as it snapped its teeth only inches from the back of the soft exposed flesh of his neck, forcing the fear down his mind raced looking for an answer, a solution and then it hit him, before the creature could figure out its mistake, Marcus hit the emergency release dropping the pack, the wolf falling backwards and landing under it with a grunt.

Before the others could react Marcus dove into the raging river. His body submerging into the cold muddy water of the rapids as pain seared his back and legs, the open wounds reacting to the frigid water, quickly the pain dissipated, the water numbing the nerves as the current carried Marcus downstream, before he could orient himself, his body slammed into the rocky bottom the water rolling him violently over the sharp rocks across the riverbed.

He struggled to orient himself, to find the surface but the river wouldn’t let him go the current pulling him down again as he fought to break the surface, again rolling him over the bottom as the half breath he managed to suck in before escaping began to burn in his lungs.

He knew he was dead, knew his only salvation would be to reach the surface as his world narrowed, all other problems a distant thought as he pulled at the water, desperately trying to reach the murky light.

His chest was on fire as his arms pulled and pulled at the water, trying to fight the strong current, he could feel the edges of his world going black, the oxygen in his lungs now gone, his body fighting for the life-giving supply just feet above him.

He felt himself getting weak, his vision going dark then suddenly he felt his hand break the surface, with all the strength he had remaining he pulled because his life depended on it and before his vision went black his head broke the surface, he sucked in air until he could hold no more, his body involuntarily gasping over and over as he fought to keep himself above the rapids. He began to regain control, treading water he oriented himself towards the far shore, as he spun, he caught the sight of the Wolves, standing on the edge of the shore further back as the rapids had carried him downstream.

The Largest one, Mother stood there looking towards Marcus, giving him that detached critical look only a predator could give to prey, her two cubs tore apart the pack with gusto, he pushed the thought out of his mind, one problem at a time he chanted realizing the few supplies he had were now gone.

Marcus paddled to the far shore, fighting the rapids and struggling to keep himself above water. After what seemed like an eternity his hand found solid ground and he crawled up onto the rocky shore, collapsing in a heap of exhaustion. He lay there for a time, his body cold he curled into a fetal position, he knew in his mind he had to move, knew he would die if he stayed here. He had to get warm, had to dry his clothes but he didn’t move, his body too heavy so he just lay there, waiting for the inevitable.

A voice pulled him from his malaise “Marcus, your chances of survival are deteriorating fast, you need to get warm, your body is going into hyper thermic shock, you need to fight it”. Snapping his head up he could see Sentinel standing there not two feet away, looking down at him with a maternal like concern.

“Fuck off” he mumbled at the machine. He stayed there for a short time, it wasn’t the words or his own motivation that finally caused him to move, it was the full body quakes that pulled him from the shore. I will not die here; I will not let this place kill me the thoughts echoing in his mind as he pulled himself towards the edge of the woods. He had to get warm, the VI is right he thought, his arms pulling the dry leaves and small branches into a pile in front of him, he reached as far as his body would allow and pulled more, the pile getting bigger as he pulled everything he could into it.

He needed warmth, needed to get dry he thought, he stared blankly at the pile for a moment, his mind barely his own as he tried to think, tried to remember I need fire he thought the convulsions making it hard to think, shifting his leg the weight of his cargo pocket caught his attention, something in one of the cargo pockets he realized, reaching in he pulled the pair of field binoculars out of his pocket, closing his eyes he said a small thank you to the universe as shaky hands began to pull the lenses from the set.

“Marcus, if you do not get warm and dry you will not survive” came the calm gentle voice of sentinel as his hands slipped from the cap as yet another set of convulsions took over his body making it next to impossible to disassemble the field glasses.

“Shut up Sentinel, you’re not helping” he said through gritted teeth, finally getting the lens off of the binoculars. He closed his eyes, steadying himself as he held the lens out, catching the light he began to shift it until a small pinpoint of light displayed on the pile in front of him. The small sliver of light shaking as he tried unsuccessfully to hold his hand still, with a curse he took a breath and tried again, steadying the light and focusing the power of the sun onto the pile.

A small whiff of smoke began to rise from the edge of a leaf, and he gently blew on it, watching the small leaf catch fire, excited he began to gently continue to breath oxygen across the pile nurturing the small flame and encouraging it to grow. He crawled as close as he dared, the small pile growing quickly as the warmth of the flames began to thaw his body, Marcus lay like that for hours, moving only to find the closest things he could burn to throw on the fire.

Day slowly turned to night as he continued to stay close to the burning pyre his mind barely present, his body trying to recover from the freezing water and cold weather.

Eventually Marcus drifted off to sleep, curled into a tight ball he did his best to stay warm as his mind drifted off.

The sound was almost expected now as he opened his eyes to the view of the rocky cliffs, listening he could hear the thrumming once again, was it closer? he wondered listening for a moment as the thrumming beat continued its death march over the horizon.

“Something is wrong fallen one, I can sense it, what has happened” came the concerned voice of the woman from behind him. Something about that voice he thought, her question was more of a command he thought turning to find the same blonde-haired beauty in that red velvet dress, standing there tall and regal in the field of tall grass only mere feet from him.

The look on her face was that of worry though, this is new he thought studying that face, what about this woman scared him he wondered as once again the hairs on his neck stood up in warning. He studied this woman, after a moment he put on his best reassuring smile “Nothing at all, what is it you want lady, how is it you can contact me like this?” he said, switching the conversation in hopes of getting answers.

She too looked up, studying his eyes, searching them she knows I am lying he thought, it wasn’t a fear, the woman did know, in fact he could feel it, could sense her conviction of that simple fact. She stopped studying him and smiled “I see you feel it, you cannot hide your intention here, you cannot obfuscate your intentions, all is known between those who use the mind bridge to communicate” she stated smiling at him. Mind Bridge he thought pulling the word apart some sort of telepathy he wondered.

“What has happened Fallen One, let me help you, tell me where you are” the woman insisted, except now Marcus could feel more than the words, but the intention as well, she truly was worried but it was not worry for another person, no it was something else and not something he understood or could put his finger on, but his instincts once again screamed at him, railed against the border of his mind, something about her was wrong he thought, something about what she is showing me, what she is telling me is not true and my mind knows it, understands an intent or instinct I cannot consciously sense he thought.

He stood there for a moment trying to get his bearing, to process this new information and ability and as he did, he could feel her holding back, she wasn’t telling him everything, so let’s take this mental shit for a test drive he thought. “What do you want with me?” he asked directly and waited, the woman looked at him confused “To find you, to help you, to protect you” she stated. The words sounded genuine, but there was something else, something there, this woman did want to find him that was true, but it wasn’t to protect him, wasn’t to help him he thought feeling the intent flow off of the words, the sensation was impossible to describe it was like tasting colors, you had no idea what it felt like until you did it.

Something in the woman shifted as her eyes narrowed in suspicion “Why won’t you let me help you?” she asked, but any sense of care or comradery was now gone, her tone was severe her words an accusation and Marcus took an involuntary step back as his mind again screamed in fear. The woman pressed, stepping forward putting herself within his personal space “I will find you fallen one, save me the time and aggravation” she said, and he could sense the truth on those words.

“Who the fuck are you lady?” Marcus spat using anger to hide his fear, hoping to put her off balance but it didn’t work, she just smiled “I am the one who will save this world fallen one, I will use whatever tools I can to ensure that we are not victim to that which your people let kill us, now tell me where you are” she finished her voice raising to scream on the last phrase and Marcus stepped back, trying to put space between them, as he did, his food found dead air and he remembered too late the cliff as he toppled, falling over the edge and speeding towards the water and rocks below.

Marcus jerked awake, his head snapping around, the smell of burning leaves filled his nose and he relaxed, As he came awake he felt the bone cold of his limbs and looked to the smoldering pile in front of him, cursing he shakily stood, walking and picking up branches and leaves, the fire had almost died and the pile of smoldering ash wasn’t enough to keep him warm. Returning to the fire he built it back up, laying down on the small warm area of the earth he thought of the woman, she meant him harm, he had seen the intent in feeling emanating off of her words and for the first time he feared finding people, finding civilization.

A lot could have changed and seemed to have in the centuries since he had walked the earth, what would he find and more importantly was he in danger, His body slowly relaxed and he returned to sleep reflecting on this and the lady by the cliff.

He woke the next morning feel off, his body hurt everywhere and a small tickle in the back of his throat refused to go away.
