After a few swallows of water, he forced himself to move. “Sentinel?” he said and could hear the rasp in his voice this isn’t good he thought, the last thing he needed now was to get sick and having spent time in the freezing water of the river and the autumn cold of night, it was looking more like his body wouldn’t recover quickly. “Yes Marcus, how many I help you?” came the friendly voice of the VI and he turned to find her behind him, standing patiently for his orders. “Based on our new location, can you navigate us to the location we previously identified” he said rubbing his temples as a headache threatened to go from bad to worse.

The VI paused and he waited as she communicated with the ship, looking around Marcus realized he was hungry and then the events of yesterday hit him. “Fuck” he whispered remembering the pack being ripped apart, his supplies eaten or destroyed, Marcus was no hunter, he had never been one to enjoy going out and shooting animals for food, not because he had anything against it, just that it was easier to go to the grocery store and he groaned at the irony of his current predicament.

Checking his belt his hands came upon the sturdy handle of the K-Bar and he sighed “Okay, I can do this” he said going over his options as he studied the forest with new eyes, that of an engineer with a problem to solve. As he was thinking through the issue Sentinel returned

“Marcus, we are still able to easily navigate to the location, the river will not pose an issue in our travels” she stated, and he nodded, at least one thing wasn’t going to be an issue he thought. As he stood there an idea began to form as he studied the small trees around him “Sentinel, can you find an offshoot of the river, slower rapids, something close by” he said, his voice slightly gravely but full of purpose as once again the VI communicated with the ship and Marcus strode to a tree, tearing off a branch, he studied it with an approving nod.

Two hours later, his body still aching Marcus found himself standing knee deep in a slow traveling tributary, holding his breath he watched the water intently as the VI floated close by “Based on the reference material we have access to, you will need to stay quiet and still, the fish will soon get used to your presence, wait until they are close before you use the spear, jabbing it straight down should garner a fish” the VI stated and Marcus shot it an annoyed look “Yes, I know, quiet” he whispered.

The spear in question was a stick that he had sharpened one end, the word spear was probably too grand for the simple stick, but it was what he had Marcus thought studying the water closely. Despite the pain in every muscle and joint he kept himself still, watching the water, trying to see under the surface as the sun distractedly played over the ripples making the task daunting. The only sound was the water lapping against the shore, the effect calming as he continued to stand there, time passed as he frustratingly watched large silver fish pass just out of reach, oblivious to the danger and his irritation as he watched them saunter by again and again.

After a while he was close to giving up, he was in the middle of rethinking his position when he looked down to see a large silver fish, floating just below him, using his legs to break the wake it just floated there, not moving as it seemed interested in something on his pants and moving in, the large fish nipped at it and then backed off. He stood there in shock for a moment just staring at it, before he remembered the hunger in his stomach and the stick which had hovered above the water shot down and into its target. With a smile and a cheer Marcus pulled the stick from the water the large fish speared through the end. “Hell yeah” he screamed to the woods, startling a flock of birds from the trees.

After eating the overcooked fish and with a smile and a full belly he started off, following the VI through the thick forest as he headed towards civilization. Using the ships ability to map the journey he was able to stay near sources of water allowing him to fish, but by the fifth day the tickle and aches in his body had grown worse. Sitting by the fire one night as the sun had set, he stared at the flames, his body launching into a coughing fit, his sides lighting up in pain as he tried to expel whatever was in his lungs.

After it subsided he pulled his hand back to reveal bloody mucus “This isn’t a good sign” he whispered, for the first time since the wolves Marcus thought he might not make it, might end up dying before he could make contact with others, before he could see what had become of his world and his people. The fever was causing him to sweat, but as soon as it touched the air it would become cold causing him to shiver, he couldn’t get warm no matter how close he got to the fire.

Three more days he traveled, barely saying a word, a zombie simply putting one foot in front of the other as the fever continued to get worse, he had stopped eating, his only sustenance was the water he forced down his throat twice a day. One foot in front of the other, he thought trying to keep himself moving despite the pain and confusion in his mind.

He walked and walked trying to keep the fear and panic of death at bay, his mind whispering to him, telling him to rest, surely death couldn’t be as bad as this it said, but Marcus ignored it, cursed it even yelled at it but still it refused to go away.

Mercifully the vision of the cliffs had not come again, thought that could have been from his inability to sleep more than anything else he thought in one of his more lucid moments.

Marcus had stopped tracking time and distance, merely walking became his whole existence, he had stopped talking to Sentinel who simply floated in front, leading him and as he faltered, the VI would slow ensuring she was always directly in his path, a beacon to salvation.

I am going to die he thought as they traveled, he didn’t know how far they had come or how close they were, but it didn’t matter, Marcus knew he would not make it. The fever had gotten worse his walking slowly progressing into merely stumbling forward, in a fevered haze he recalled an argument, he begged the woman who stood In front of him to save him, to take him home, the world soon went dark and when Marcus woke, Sentinel’s egg lay scattered across the ground in pieces, he cried for an hour until he could no longer recall why he was crying or for whom, and he continued on his journey, forever walking, forever moving in a mental haze.

Shuffling, staring at the ground as his mind tried to decide if laying down, giving in would be so bad, he could simply lay down for a moment he thought, when suddenly the sun became brighter as the trees opened up above, surprised Marcus stopped and looked up and then around, something about this called to him, tried to get his attention but his mind was muddy, unable to form a clear thought and so he stood there staring blankly around as his body swayed.

Suddenly a sound started in the distance, something hitting the ground and he cocked his head was that really a sound or something his mind had created he wondered.

It wasn’t the first time since becoming sick that his mind had played tricks on him, he thought closing his eyes, listening to the sound as it began to grow progressively louder.

There was something familiar about it he thought listening intently as his body continued to sway with fever, he had heard that before, but where. Turning he caught sight of motion and his eyes went wide, as he tried to process the sight through the fog of fever, two horses with riders bore down on him. They rode fast as he continued to just stand there his addled mind not able to process the sight and then just as quickly, they passed, one turned and called back something in a language he didn’t understand but the sentiment was clear.

“Help” he tried to call, his voice a raspy whisper as the riders disappeared around the bend, looking down he noticed the worn ground, a simple dirt road, this had been what had stopped him, his unconscious mind understanding the meaning before he did.

There are people near he thought as adrenaline coursed through his system, temporarily clearing the fevered fog in his mind, his body barley responding exhausted and malnourished, the hope was the only thing fueling him. He wasn’t going to die, Marcus turned towards where the riders had emerged and began to shamble in that direction. Moving along the road, he began noticing the old derelict fencing shadowing him as he walked, guiding him up the worn dirt road.

The sun began to settle beyond the horizon as he came over a hill, stopping suddenly, his mind trying to assure him it wasn’t a mirage or another hallucination, the sight bringing a tear to his eye as in the distance, stood a simple wood cabin surrounded with small pens for animals and fields stretching behind it far into the distance as rows of plants swayed gently in the evening breeze, a farm he thought, picking up his pace, moving towards the first sign of salvation and civilization since landing. The small home grew closer as he began to take in the details of structure, the hand laid shingles and simple poles holding up a crooked porch, the mostly even thatch roof, his eyes roved over the other structures, pausing as he studied the old two story barn and finally the pens holding familiar animals like cows and pigs the sight bringing a smile to his face as he turned into the open gate of the mostly fallen property fence and made his way to the door.

Laying a foot on the step he listened as it protested his weight, Marcus climbed the stairs and shambling across the small porch he found himself out of breath and needing to lean on the frame for a moment before coming to stand before the worn wooden door, gathering himself, Marcus turned and knocked. He could hear the sound echo through the home, judging by the lights in the windows, someone was home and then he heard movement, someone slowly approaching the door, pausing for a moment and Marcus thought he could hear breathing, he listened intently as metal scraped metal and the large door opened a crack, revealing a large green eye and pale skin of a woman. For a moment Marcus was lost, he didn’t know what to say and simply stood there gawking at another human, tears now freely streaming down his cheeks.

Finally, he took a step forward “Help me, please, I am sick” he said and took another shambling step towards the heavy door. Suddenly it shut and he heard the movement of the locks as the door was barred against him.

Marcus simply collapsed, he had no energy, no ability to do more as the sickness finally overwhelmed him, he drifted into a fevered darkness.
